thread.title: Tech Today: Google's Record Fine, Dumping Broadcom, Twitter, ASML Surges - Nasdaq.com

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Google's Record Fine, Dumping Broadcom, Twitter, ASML Surges - Nasdaq.com
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Alphabet Up Despite €4.3 Billion EU Fine Shares of Alphabet ( GOOGL ) are up $3.31, or 0.27%, to $1,216.40 after the European Union imposed a €4.3 billion fine on the company's Google unit for anti-trust violations in the way that it struck deals with phone makers for use of its Android software that "denied rivals the chance to innovate and compete," in the words of Margarethe Vestager, the EU competition commission, as reported by Bloomberg's Aoife White , Stephanie Bodoni , and Natalia Drozdiak .
Google has 90 days to top "illegal practices," the authors relate.
Google's CEO, Sundar Pichai , posted an essay online in which he said the ruling ignores the fact Android compete's with Apple 's ( AAPL ) iOS software, and that Android provides opportunity to "thousands of phone makers" and "millions of app developers."
"We intend to appeal," he wrote.
And Google has its defenders this morning: Credit Suisse 's Stephen Ju writes that " consumers have already made their choice " based on many having chosen Google's search and browser software on the desktop before even going to mobile, and using them on Apple's iOS.
"From a debundling impact perspective on the business, we expect minimal impact as the consumer is likely to just simply download the apps for Google's services if and when they get new Android phones-much as they already do on when they get new iPhones."
Google's Pain Amazon's Gain? Also writing today, R.W. Baird 's Colin Sebastian thinks this is a big win for Amazon.com ( AMZN ). He notes that Vestager specifically cited Google as a source of Amazon's "Fire" line of Android devices failing in the marketplace.
"To force Google to support distribution of forked-versions of Android (which Google does not control) could directly benefit Amazon's Fire devices," writes Sebastian.
"To use the example cited by Margrethe Vestager in the press conference, the EC argues that Fire smartphones were not commercially successful because Google did not allow manufacturers to pre-install Google apps on those devices (forget the fact that the apps wouldn't work as well, or at all, on a modified OS.)"
Amazon shares are down $4.42 to $1,839.51.
Big Blue's Q2 International Business Machines ( IBM ) reports Q2 results this afternoon, after the closing bell, and the Street is, on average, expecting $19.85 billion in revenue and $3.04 per share in net income.
Toni Sacconaghi of Bernstein , who has a Market Perform rating on IBM shares, writes that this should be an "in-line" performance, and he raises his the concern he's expressed previously, that IBM will struggle to reach its forecast $13.80 per share in net income this year.
"We suspect that IBM will find non-operating items (e.g. likely further tax discrete tax benefits) to achieve its EPS guidance for the year," he writes, and he advises investors to pay attention to the company's details this evening about its services profit margin, its software rate of revenue growth, its "signings" in services, and the backlog there, and also how its " strategic imperatives "-things such as cloud computing-are growing.
Note that eBay ( EBAY ) is also reporting this evening.
IBM shares are up 7 cents at $143.56, while eBay is up 28 cents, or 0.8% at $38.10.
All Hail Rich Templeton Shares of Texas Instruments (TXN) are down $1.14, or 1%, at $114.66, after the company last night said its CEO , Brian Crutcher , is resigning after the company determined he violated the company's code of conduct. The former CEO of 14 years, Rich Templeton, is stepping in, for what appears a permanent appointment, which is encouraging to most on the Street today given he's regarded as one of the best CEOs in the industry.
TI also pre-announced Q2 results that topped expectations.
Mark Lipacis of Jefferies & Co . cheers "Who better than Rich?"
Reiterating his Buy rating, and $150 price target, Lipacis writes, "Templeton led the transformation of TXN to an Analog and Embedded processing powerhouse, as well as to a best-in-class generator of cash flow and returner of capital to shareholders."
"Our sense is that most consider him one of the top CEOs in the history of the industry."
Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein , who rates the stock at Outperform, writes Templeton's return "should act to calm investors (he is hugely respected, and was after all in the role only 6 weeks ago)."
Rasgon thinks the situation is "considerably more benign than other recent CEO changes in the semiconductor industry," referring to Intel 's (INTC) abrupt dismissal of Brian Krzanich a month ago.
"Intel's CEO firing comes at a time of considerable strategic flux for them, and opens them up for a potentially lengthy and messy succession, neither of which appear to be an issue for TXN in this situation."
Cutting Broadcom Broadcom Inc. Shares of Broadcom (AVGO) are up $1.34, or 0.6%, at $209.65, despite a downgrade at Goldman Sachs , by analyst Toshiya Hari , who cut the stock to Neutral from Buy, and cut the firm's price target to $220 from $300, after concluding that there is just too much uncertainty in the company's proposed acquisition of CA (CA), announced last week.
Hari has numerous questions, such as whether the combined company will "be a diversified semiconductor company or will it become more of a software company long-term?"
"We believe management will need to provide greater clarity on its forward strategy," writes Hari, and that it will take time for management to gain investors' confidence in their ability to achieve their goals."
Hari is also worried about Broadcom's " core " business of RF semiconductors , given that the company's been losing share in Apple's iPhone to Qorvo (QRVO).
Twitter's User Problem Shares of Twitter ( TWTR ) are down $1.77, or almost 4%, to $42.94, after Macquarie 's Ben Schachter cut his rating on the shares to Neutral from Buy, while raising his price target to $42 from $36, after concluding the company's user base is not growing fast enough even though Twitter is "executing" better than in past.
Schachter is "concerned" that "overall usage trends are not improving more rapidly."
"Despite Trump being perhaps the most high-profile user possible, usage has not dramatically improved over the past couple of years (the US had flat y/y growth in 1Q'18)," he observes.
"We simply don't see the product improvements having a dramatic impact on TWTR's ability to attract new users (though it can, and likely is, helping to retain and improve the experience for current users).
"We hope to be proven wrong in terms of TWTR's ability to attract new users, but want to see more proof."
ASML Surges on Surprise Q2 Beat Shares of chip-equipment maker ASML (ASML) are up $12.77, or over 6%, to $217.11, after the company this morning reported Q2 revenue and profit that comfortably topped expectations, delivering €2.74 billion in revenue and €1.37 per share in net income against consensus of €2.56 billion and €1.21 per share.
The company's forecast also came in higher than expected. CEO Peter Wennink said the company shipped one more device than expected in the quarter, and is "on track" with a goal of shipping 20 systems this year.
"After an excellent first half of 2018, we expect the second half to be stronger," said Wennink.
This is a stock that had been under a cloud of worry about potential hiccups in its shipment of equipment, given Intel 's (INTC) production issues of late. Bernstein analyst Mark Li last month wrote the company was in something of a bubble of its own making.
Robert Maire of Semiconductor Advisors calls the report "superb," and while orders for the company's machines declined in the quarter, "we still think that the solid backlog will allow the company to continue to ship at a relatively steady rate."
C.J. Muse of Evercore ISI said report will come as a surprise to many given the "push outs" of equipment ordering that had been widely observed in recent weeks .
He was not surprised, Muse writes, as delays at Samsung Electronics ( 005930KS ) were predictably made up for by competitor SK Hynix ( 000660KS ).
Going forward, more and more wafers need to be added for things such as DRAM production, "Thus, moving to 2019, all signs from management suggest positive trends will continue."
